qsm-secrets pipe.description: Run a consumer with the key's value on its stdin; the command follows a -- separator, so this verb is reached from a shell, not from the noun

qsm-secrets env.description: Run a consumer with the key's value in one environment variable; the command follows a -- separator, so this verb is reached from a shell, not from the noun

qsm-secrets set.description: Store a new key; the value is typed into the vault's own prompt and is never an argument or stdin

args.name: key
args.description: the key name to store under

args.name: gui
args.description: collect the value in the askpass pane instead of the terminal; the value goes to the backend and never to the caller

qsm-secrets askpass.description: Ask the person for one answer in the askpass pane and give it to the consumer that asked: sudo -A, ssh and git take the typed text on stdout, decide takes a hook-kit ask request on stdin and answers allow or deny; run through the qsm-askpass-<kind> links the install makes, the consumer's words follow a -- separator

args.name: kind
args.description: secret, sudo, ssh, git or decide

args.name: folder
args.description: the namespace to write, for the secret kind (default: qsm)

qsm-secrets askpass enable.description: Print the fish lines that point SUDO_ASKPASS, SSH_ASKPASS, GIT_ASKPASS or HOOK_KIT_ASKPASS at the installed links; it writes nothing, the person puts them in their own config

qsm-secrets has.description: Report whether the key is stored: ok when it is, missing when it is not; never a value

qsm-secrets list.description: Print the key names this wrapper stored, never a value: in one namespace, or as <namespace>/<key> in every namespace when none is named

args.name: folder
args.description: the namespace to read (default: QSM_SECRETS_FOLDER, else every namespace)

qsm-secrets inspect.description: Print name, username and folder for every entry in the namespace, whoever stored it; never a value

qsm-secrets rm.description: Remove a stored key and its capture index row; reports missing rather than a silent success when it was not stored

qsm-secrets rename.description: Rename a stored key without its value leaving this process: the new entry is written and read back equal before the old one is removed, a capture index row moves with it, and an existing target is refused

args.name: folder
args.description: the namespace of the stored key (default: qsm)

args.name: toFolder
args.description: the namespace to move it to (default: the same namespace; with --legacy, qsm)

args.name: legacy
args.description: the source is an entry stored before namespaces existed (libsecret only), so it has no namespace

qsm-secrets prune.description: Remove captured entries whose id no session transcript under ~/.claude/projects names, and their capture index rows; prints each id, never a value

args.name: dryRun
args.description: only list the ids that would be removed

qsm-secrets check.description: Run a probe with the key's value in one environment variable, discard its output and report ok or failed with its exit code; the command follows a -- separator, so this verb is reached from a shell, not from the noun

qsm-secrets get.description: Write the value to file descriptor 3, which the caller opens; refuses when it is closed

qsm-secrets guard.description: Read a Bash command on stdin and refuse it, as blocked with a code and the verb to use instead, when it would put a stored credential into a tool result: a vault or keyring reader, the secret service on the bus, the keyring or vault data files, a rendered config file, a keyring library, the descriptor-3 channel pointed at the output, or a placeholder inside single quotes; the command is read from its syntax tree, through wrappers, subshells and pipelines

qsm-secrets capture.description: Read a prompt piped on stdin, store each secret in it (a known token shape, a value after a credential name, or a random 32-character token that is no path, name, id or hash) in the active backend under a generated id, or under its own name for a pasted name=value, and print the text with each value replaced by {{secret:<id>}} (or {{secret:qsm/<name>}}) and, for a long secret, its last four characters; each stored secret gets a row in the capture index: its kind, the time, the session and the working directory, never a value

args.name: session
args.description: the session id the capture is recorded under

args.name: cwd
args.description: the working directory the capture is recorded under

qsm-secrets captures.description: List what the capture stored, newest first: namespace/key, kind, time, session and working directory, never a value; a row whose entry is no longer stored is removed from the index with a warning

qsm-secrets mask.description: Read text piped on stdin and print it with each named id's stored value replaced by its {{secret:<id>}} placeholder; with --all, read a JSON array of strings and mask every stored value of every namespace in each, with one backend read

args.name: id
args.description: a captured id whose value is masked

args.name: all
args.description: mask every stored value of every namespace in a JSON array of strings on stdin; prints the array

qsm-secrets scrub.description: Replace every stored value that is still in a transcript, and in its subagents' transcripts, with its placeholder, by rewriting each file atomically; never prints a value

args.name: transcript
args.description: a transcript path, or a session id, found as <id>.jsonl under ~/.claude/projects

args.name: detach
args.description: start the scrub in a detached process and return at once

qsm-secrets render.description: Write a template with each {{secret:<id>}} or {{secret:<namespace>/<key>}} filled in to a file only this session's user can read, under XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, and print its path

args.name: out
args.description: the rendered file's name inside the session directory

qsm-secrets clean.description: Remove the session's directory with every file rendered into it

qsm-secrets doctor.description: Probe every prerequisite the other verbs depend on and name the fix for each failed check
